questions: For each index i, should we output a single integer representing the maximum possible GCD among all valid K‑element subsets that contain A_i, or something else?
If multiple K‑element subsets containing A_i yield the same optimal GCD, does it matter which one we consider, or is only the GCD value required?
When K = 1, is the answer for each i simply A_i, or should we treat this case differently?
Must the K chosen elements be distinct positions in the original sequence, or can the same value appear multiple times if it occurs at different indices?
Should the output be N space‑separated integers on one line, N lines each containing one integer, or another format?
Are there any constraints on the order of processing i (e.g., must we output answers in increasing i), or can they be printed in any order?
If N is large (up to 1.2 × 10⁶), are there any time or memory limits implied that affect the required algorithmic complexity?
Are the input numbers guaranteed to fit in standard 32‑bit signed integers, or should we use larger integer types for intermediate GCD calculations?

For each i = 1, 2, \dots, N, solve the following problem: When you choose K elements from A that include A_i, find the maximum possible GCD (greatest common divisor) of those chosen elements. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print the result. Constraints - 1 \leq K \leq N \leq 1.2 \times 10^6 - 1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6 - All input values are integers.
